title: Influence of viral seroprevalence on postoperative outcome in relation to different anesthetic techniques
summary: Viruses can cause respiratory infections. The immune system responds to these viruses by producing antibodies that fight them, which helps us recover. The amount of these antibodies differs from person to person. To investigate why some people become ill after surgery, the antibodies of each patient will be measured and compared.
conditions: postoperative respiratory tract infections, wound infections or other infections

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- ASA physical status I–III
- Elective surgery
- Surgery involving the upper airway, head or neck
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy
- Participants unable to give informed consent
- Age < 18 years
- Non-elective surgery
- HIV infection
- Use of immunosuppressive medication
